summary: SCOPED CLAIM — the context-indicator DENOMINATOR in tools/governor/sampler.mjs and its test, AFTER a prior review of this same scope returned request_changes. Scoped deliberately to match the diff shown; the wider BUILD-018 teardown is reviewed under separate claims. HISTORY YOU SHOULD KNOW, because it is the reason this packet exists. A first repair matched a denominator by MODEL ID and added two heuristics (refuse when matched observations disagree; treat a bare id as ambiguous when a variant-suffixed sibling exists). Your prior review found TQA-001 HIGH: those heuristics are contingent on the store happening to contain a sibling, so on a fresh store the original defect is fully live. That finding was CONFIRMED by execution and is the direct cause of this change. Your own X3 phrasing was adopted as the governing principle: agreement between observations establishes store consistency, NOT live-session identity. WHAT THIS DIFF DOES. Cross-session inference is DELETED, not patched. resolveWindowTokens no longer takes modelId at all, no longer enumerates the store directory, and no longer groups sizes by id. It reads exactly one record — the one keyed by the LIVE session id — because the session id is the only link that establishes identity between a transcript sample and a statusLine observation of the same runtime; every other link is similarity. Guards (a) DISAGREEMENT and (b) VARIANT AMBIGUITY are deleted along with variantBaseOf and its regex, because a rule that never matches across sessions cannot suffer a cross-namespace match; keeping them would be a heuristic guarding a rule that no longer exists. Guard (c) SELF-CONTRADICTION survives on its own merits — it is arithmetic, not inference, and it is the only guard that also binds the explicit-operator route. Guard (d) IDENTITY is added: the record's own session_id must equal the one asked for, asserted rather than assumed. CARRY-FORWARD, and why it is not a loophole: the health store is one file per session and a transcript write REPLACES the whole file, flipping source to transcript, so a same-session rule accepting only source==statusLine would go BLIND after the first Stop hook of every turn. The carried context_window_size is therefore accepted, but ONLY when its recorded context_window_source is statusline-observed and never when it was env-declared, since the env is re-read on every call and carrying it would keep an operator's statement alive after the operator withdrew it. BEHAVIOURAL CONSEQUENCE, stated because it is a real product cost and not hidden: web and mobile clients, where the terminal statusLine never runs, now get a TRUE token count and NO graded percentage unless CLAUDE_CONTEXT_WINDOW is set. That is a tightening. The percentage they previously saw was borrowed from an unrelated session's terminal and was wrong by up to five-fold; nothing true is lost. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: tools/governor/continuity.mjs and tools/governor/continuity-derive.mjs have NO TESTS AT ALL — zero coverage, not merely unproven wiring; nothing in this diff has run in CI, all counts are from one Windows machine; no live host was exercised, so the assumption that a terminal's statusLine renders at least once before its first Stop hook is plausible and UNVERIFIED — if false, turn 1 is BLIND and self-heals at turn 2; a mid-session model change can leave a same-session observation stale and is a stated residual, deliberately NOT guarded because such a guard would re-import the deleted variant logic; and a record already on disk keeps its old baked-in denominator until rewritten. All evidence behind this is builder self-test plus the orchestrator's own re-run. It is NOT independent review, which is what you are being asked for.
brief_excerpt:
Judge this diff against these acceptance criteria and ONLY these.

SCOPE: this packet contains tools/governor/sampler.mjs and tools/governor/sampler.test.mjs ONLY. Two notes so a scope artefact is not mistaken for a defect. (1) Rows about any other file are OUT OF SCOPE — mark them not_applicable, never blocked, and do not let the absence of other files reduce confidence in the rows below. (2) The end-to-end seam test that carries a real sampler output through footer derivation and rendering lives in tools/governor/footer.test.mjs, which is NOT in this packet and is reviewed separately. A previous review of this scope reported that seam test as missing; it exists, and the fault was the claim's, not the code's. Do not re-report it.

H1. Cross-session inference must be GONE, not merely constrained. resolveWindowTokens must not take modelId, must not enumerate the store directory, and must not group or compare observations across sessions. Verify by reading the code, not the comments.
H2. A denominator may come only from (i) an explicit operator-declared window, or (ii) the record keyed by the LIVE session id. Nothing else.
H3. Guard (d) IDENTITY: the returned record's own session_id must be checked against the one requested, not assumed to match because the filename did.
H4. Guard (c) SELF-CONTRADICTION survives and still binds BOTH routes, including the explicit-operator one.
H5. Guards (a) and (b) and variantBaseOf must be DELETED, not retained as defence in depth. A heuristic guarding a rule that no longer exists is dead code that will be mistaken for protection later. Explanatory comments recording why they went are correct and are not a violation.
H6. CARRY-FORWARD is accepted ONLY when the carried context_window_source is statusline-observed. An env-declared value must NEVER be carried forward, because the env is re-read each call and a carried copy would outlive its withdrawal.
H7. THE FEATURE MUST REMAIN REACHABLE. Verify from the tests that a denominator still resolves for: an explicit operator declaration; this session's own statusLine observation; and that same value AFTER a transcript write has replaced the file. A repair that returns null everywhere satisfies H1 while destroying the feature. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE ROW — it is the one a lazy fix passes and a correct one must earn.
H8. NO REGRESSION OF TQA-001. Construct the case yourself from the code: a store holding another session's observation, and a live session with a different true window. It must yield no denominator.

ADVERSARIAL ROWS — answer even if every row above passes:
Y1. Is there ANY input for which a denominator is returned that was not established for the live session? Name it concretely. This is the third attempt at this class of defect; assume it is still present and try to find it.
Y2. Does the same-session rule make the feature unreachable in a realistic configuration NOT covered by H7?
Y3. Carry-forward re-admits a value written by an earlier process. Can that be abused or confused — by session-id reuse, a stale file, a clock problem, or a record whose provenance field disagrees with its content?
Y4. The store is keyed by a directory derived from the working directory. Does anything here behave surprisingly when one session's statusLine and its hook resolve to different directories?

OUT OF SCOPE - do not report as defects: which modules were kept or deleted (the operator's decision); prose, naming or comment-style preference; concrete model-id literals used as TEST FIXTURES (a prior review flagged these against an over-broad criterion; the constraint binds the SOURCE, which an existing source-scan test already enforces); the absence of malicious-handler hardening, since this estate's bar is correctness, accidental leak, availability and audit for a first-party personal system; the lack of CI execution and the zero test coverage of continuity.mjs, both disclosed above and already recorded.
